chapters.title: A Day at the Beach
covers: Counts shells, boats and fruit at a seashore picture by making groups instead of one by one
Writes how many tens and loose ones are in a bunch of bananas or a string of shells
Splits 25, 43, 35 and 58 chikoos into trays of ten and the rest
Lists things that come in packs of ten
Matches a number of chikoos to the trays and loose fruit that make it up, with blocks and strips for ten and one

chapters.title: Shapes Around Us
topics: 3D shapes: cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere
covers: Looks at musical instruments and finds which ones match the shape of a drum or a matka
Matches everyday objects with the solid shape each one is closest to
Finds the odd shape out among a set of objects
Explains how instruments are played, by beating, plucking or blowing
Talks about how a harmonium's shape differs from a drum's

chapters.title: Fun with Numbers
covers: Counts beads on a ginladi (bead frame) and makes number cards for numbers like 38 or 98
Moves along a number strip, forward and backward, to reach a target number
Plays a guessing game where yes or no questions narrow down a secret number
Finds the numbers on a number chart that a skip-counting frog lands on
Completes number patterns and says what comes before a number

chapters.title: Shadow Story
covers: Makes animal shapes with their hands and acts out a shadow play
Notes when shadows appear and when they disappear
Changes the position of a torch and sees how the shadow changes
Compares shadow length at different times of the day
Traces the outline of everyday objects such as a bottle cap or eraser and matches traces

chapters.title: Playing with Lines
covers: Sorts yoga poses by the lines they make: standing, sleeping, slanting or curved
Holds a thread taut and then slacken it to see straight and not-straight lines
Traces missing lines in a picture
Makes new shapes using straight lines drawn on dot grids

chapters.title: Decoration for Festival
covers: Completes a table of flowers in garlands, showing tens and ones for each child
Adds two numbers by adding tens and ones separately, such as 10 + 2 and 50 + 3
Works out 25 + 12 and 57 + 34 by counting on or using a number line
Solves sums like 24 + 43 by breaking one number into tens and ones
Adds blocks or sticks that two friends have collected

chapters.title: Rani's Gift
topics: non-standard units such as hand spans
covers: Works out why a carpenter's bed measured in hand spans came out different
Estimates and then measures the length of a desk, a blackboard and a window with a textbook
Finds the shortest path from home to school, marking it on a picture
Picks the longest and shortest path between two points and checks with a thread

chapters.title: Grouping and Sharing
covers: Counts wheels of autorickshaws, cars and bicycles by adding equal groups
Writes repeated addition as multiplication, for example 4 times 2 is 8
Fills in the number of groups and items in each group for butterflies, octopuses and soldiers
Builds tables of 2, 3, 5 and 10 by counting groups
Notices that 4 groups of 3 and 3 groups of 4 give the same total

chapters.title: Which Season Is It?
covers: Reads a calendar for the year and sorts months by how many days they have
Counts days in a week and adds days to find a total
Discusses which seasons they like and why, and which festivals fall in each season
Says whether an activity takes days, hours or months, such as cooking or growing a plant
Learns the names of seasons in Hindi and other languages

chapters.title: Fun at the Fair
topics: rupees and paise in everyday use
covers: Works out how much was spent on rides by adding the cost of each ride
Finds money left by subtracting spending from the amount given
Checks a friend's spending by adding back the amounts spent
Finds the cost of rides using tickets, for example 2 tickets at 15 rupees each
Learns the larger notes in common use

chapters.title: Data Handling
topics: comparing counts with more than and less than
covers: Counts favourite colours and fruits in a picture and fills in a table
Reads a chart of how students come to school, such as on foot, by bus or by bicycle
Says which item is liked most and least, and compares counts
Reads a table of games played and fills in the blanks
Surveys the families of classmates and records how many people live in each home
